subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` remain a supported hard-enforcement surface for Telegram DMs, and should it be implemented through a shared direct-aware tool-policy resolver?
rationale: The schema and types already advertise a security-sensitive tool-policy surface, but current runtime enforcement does not read that direct config; enforcement versus retirement changes operator security expectations and config compatibility.

options.title: Enforce Direct DM Tool Policy
options.body: Treat the existing Telegram direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with isolation and precedence tests.

options.title: Retire The Accepted Surface
options.body: If maintainers do not want DM-level hard enforcement, reject or migrate the direct tool-policy fields through doctor/docs so operators do not rely on a silent no-op.

options.title: Defer To Broader Binding Policy
options.body: Keep this blocked on the broader per-binding policy design while accepting that Telegram direct policy remains unreliable until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct DM Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Treat the existing Telegram direct `tools` and `toolsBySender` fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with isolation and precedence tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent history in group tool-policy inheritance and per-sender policy work, and the choice spans security boundary and product contract semantics.
